reason: E1 confirms coherent, ordered nanoprecipitates in a related alloy but reports an average volume corresponding to a diameter well above 50 nm, not below it. E2 describes 91 nm coherent particles that enhance strength without increasing coercivity, contradicting the premise that only sub-50 nm sizes avoid pinning. The cited evidence does not support the specific size threshold, the annealing control, or the direct link to enhanced magnetocaloric effect.
premises: Coherent nanoprecipitates below ~50 nm do not significantly pin domain walls, preserving low hysteresis.
The Fe–Co–Ni–Ta–Al alloy system can form coherent, ordered nanoprecipitates.
Nanoprecipitate size can be controlled via annealing to remain below the domain wall width.
Fine precipitates enhance magnetocaloric effect by reducing energy barriers during field cycling.
A precipitate size threshold exists (~50 nm) below which coercivity remains <11 Oe and refrigerant capacity improves.
